brief: Goldman's US equities desk reads Monday's bounce (S&P +60bps to 7,722; NDX +129bps to 29,651 on back-to-back 1%+ gains for the first time in ~3 months; R2K +117bps; Dow +3bps) as driven mainly by supply-abatement (short covering/de-grossing easing) rather than fresh buying, per Peter Bartlett, with only limited, newly emerging buying ('offense') in the AI complex. Breadth was narrow (~60% of S&P names lower) and floor activity stayed low (4/10, skews benign), though the momentum factor rose 2.5% off its ~20% drawdown and GSPRHIMO is up ~8% over three sessions even as GSPB L/S momentum exposure sits near YTD lows post-degrossing. Options flow turned bullish in tech/hyperscalers (SPY, AAPL, GOOGL call buying), and the desk believes the market has rallied back into dealer long gamma, now hunting a catalyst to hold SPX above 7700. Bartlett's base case stays choppy pending more price stability before a fuller risk-on tilt, with tomorrow's Fed decision (SPX implied move 61bps, up from 50bps) the next test. Separately, STX fell 7% post-bell in a 'sell the news' reaction despite beating and guiding revenue +14% q/q.
